bull.b: Persistent positive operating and free cash flow (TTM ~$616M) provides durable self-funding capacity for product investments and marketing, reducing reliance on external capital. This cash generation supports scaling Predictions and DKeX while cushioning earnings volatility and refinancing needs.

Sustained high customer adds with materially improved CAC indicate durable improvement in unit economics. More efficient acquisition drives higher LTV/CAC, enables scale with lower marginal marketing spend, and supports long-term revenue growth and margin expansion as cohorts monetize over time.

Rapid Predictions adoption plus DKeX and FCM approval create a structurally different revenue stream and improved take-rates. Vertical integration enhances unit economics, captures more margin, and lessens dependence on third-party exchanges, supporting sustainable revenue diversification over the medium term.

bear.b: Leverage above 3x equity increases sensitivity to operating swings and reduces financial flexibility. High debt heightens refinancing and interest-rate risk, constrains strategic optionality for M&A or buybacks, and makes the firm more vulnerable to revenue or margin softness over the next several quarters.

bear.t: Inconsistent profitability and recent net loss
bear.b: Return to net losses despite multi-year scale shows profitability is not yet durable. Episodic operating losses undermine confidence in converting scale into persistent profits, complicate servicing of elevated debt, and mean free cash flow can be volatile if revenue or hold deteriorates.

bear.t: Regulatory and execution uncertainty for Predictions
bear.b: Predictions faces structural regulatory and execution risk that can delay rollouts or require product changes. That uncertainty raises the odds of slower-than-expected ROI on the $200M–$300M ramp, increases compliance costs, and could limit long-term contribution to adjusted EBITDA.
